hero.label: CONSTRUCTION & TRAINING PROVIDERS
hero.headline: Nobody tells you when something has run out. Until it stops a job.
hero.subhead: Insurance, cards, method statements and certificates all expire on different dates. Most firms track them on a spreadsheet, so the first you hear of a lapse is when a job can't start or a client asks for proof. We make sure you know first, and take the chasing off your managers.

results.title: You're told before anything expires.
results.text: Insurance, cards and certificates are flagged in good time, not found out on the day.

results.title: Jobs that start on time.
results.text: Every subcontractor's documents are in, and in date, before day one.

results.title: Managers who manage.

results.title: Proof ready when the client asks.
results.text: Tender and audit evidence in one place, found in minutes.

results.title: People ready in 30 minutes, not three days.

problems.title: The spreadsheet doesn't warn you.
problems.text: Managers describe spending whole days chasing subcontractors for renewed insurance, tracked on a spreadsheet nobody has time to open.

problems.title: Jobs that can't start.
problems.text: 59% of large UK construction firms have had a start on site delayed by a day or more because documents were missing.

problems.title: Lost tenders.
problems.text: One in five large UK construction firms has lost a tender, or been marked down, because it couldn't produce compliance evidence fast enough.

problems.title: The big systems aren't made for smaller firms.
problems.text: Small firms reviewing the best-known construction platform call it costly and not made for a company their size.

problems.title: Not enough people.
problems.text: UK construction needs about 206,000 more workers by 2030.

problems.title: Too many systems.
problems.text: Training providers commonly run across a learner system, an ePortfolio, a CRM, finance software and spreadsheets.

usualFix: The big construction platforms are built for large main contractors, and smaller firms find them too costly and too much. So the checking falls back on a spreadsheet, and a spreadsheet can't tell you when something is about to lapse. Learner systems have the same gap for training providers: they report to funders, but they don't chase a missing document. We build that missing part around how your organisation works.

faqs.q: Do we have to replace the systems we already use?
faqs.a: No. We fix the part they don't cover and work alongside them.

faqs.q: Does it work for subcontractors as well as employees?
faqs.a: Yes. It is built around whoever you put on site.

faqs.q: Will it help when a client or auditor asks for evidence?
faqs.a: Yes. Everything is kept in one place, so it takes minutes to pull together.
The first part is usually live in six to eight weeks.
We agree one fixed price before any work starts.
